Subject: Re: MAP exploration — prompt pack/testcases

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Acme ML is keen to run a short evaluation with Redwood to validate throughput/quality tradeoffs on our prompt suite. Procurement asked that we formalize a Mutual Action Plan so their legal and security teams can review clear acceptance gates and retention rules before we exchange any non-public testcases.

High level asks from my side:
- Can we get a 4-week sandbox loan of your latest prompt pack + ~1k testcases?
- Acceptance gate: agreement on 100 sample testcases + pass/fail rubric before broader access.
- Usage constraints: ephemeral copies only, no re-distribution, automatic destruction after the evaluation window.

I attached a sample prompt index to give you a sense of the format. Happy to loop in Procurement/Legal.

Cheers,
Samir

Samir — thanks for the clear notes. We can absolutely run this as a short MAP-driven pilot. Proposed operational checkpoints below (we'll formalize in a short MPA doc and DocuSign):

1) Week 0 (onboarding): sign MPA + NDAs; Redwood provides a zipped, read-only prompt pack and 100 sample testcases in a staging bucket.
2) Week 1 (seed validation): Acme reviews 100 sample testcases and returns acceptance rubric feedback within 3 business days.
3) Week 2–3 (run): Full 1k testcase loan into an ephemeral sandbox (no external egress). Logs and aggregated metrics accessible via the Console; no raw testcase export.
4) Week 4 (close): Acceptance run and either (a) transition to paid pilot or (b) destruction and confirmation of wipe.

Constraints/notes:
- We require a signed limited-use license (promptpack-license.txt) covering ephemeral evaluation rights.
- Default retention for any provided dataset is 90 days unless otherwise agreed; we can shorten to 30 days for highly sensitive samples if Procurement requires.
- For regressions/quality checks, we recommend a pinned small eval model variant; fallback policies are documented in the MPA.

Attaching a draft MAP and the license text for your legal team's review. Marissa/Ben: can you confirm SLA for sandbox availability and the Console access level?

Best,
Olga Petrov
